title: Portugal, 1497
hook: Portuguese Jews are forcibly converted en masse

segments.voice: Yesterday, Don Isaac Abravanel, the minister who refused to be saved alone. Your line was he left with them. Today, the road west, to the next border.

For exiles in western Spain, the nearest way out was not the sea. It was Portugal, just next door. Families who had left Spain crossed into it with what they could carry, and for a short while it looked like a refuge. They had paid to enter. They spoke a language close to their own. Then a new king of Portugal arranged a royal marriage with the house of Spain, and the terms of that marriage reached the refugees. The door they had walked through was about to become a trap.
screen: `THE BORDER NEXT DOOR.` → `A SHORT REFUGE.` → `A ROYAL MARRIAGE.`

segments.voice: King Manuel ordered the Jews of Portugal to leave, then made it almost impossible to go. Chroniclers of the time, Jewish and Christian, tell what followed. Children were taken from their parents to be baptized and raised as Christians. Adults gathered at the port of Lisbon, waiting for the promised ships, were baptized by force instead. Spain had at least offered a choice. Here the choice was made for them. Samuel Usque, a Jewish writer of the next generation, wrote a book of consolation for these families, and tells of parents who grieved for children carried away. Those who came out of this were called New Christians. Some became Christians in heart; others kept what they could of Judaism in secret, and in Portugal some kept it a very long time. In the twentieth century an engineer named Samuel Schwarz met families in the hills of the north who still said their own prayers by heart, in Portuguese, and wrote them down. Jewish law holds that a person acting under force is not to blame, and rabbis applied that to the anusim, the forced ones, though they argued over those who later could have left and stayed. Psalm forty-four speaks for people who suffer and still hold on: "All this is come upon us; yet have we not forgotten Thee." They tried not to forget. And their descendants would turn up later in this story, in other ports, asking to come home to a Judaism their families had carried in secret.
screen: `AN ORDER TO LEAVE, AND NO WAY OUT.` · `BAPTIZED BY FORCE.` · `NEW CHRISTIANS, SOME IN SECRET.` · then, large: `YET HAVE WE NOT FORGOTTEN.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a parent at a harbor, waiting for a ship that never came. Then widen the picture to anyone you know of who was made to give up something they loved: a language, a name, a faith, a home. Remembering is the whole practice, and if you pray, you can say the psalm's line: yet have we not forgotten Thee.
Portugal. The refuge next door that closed: Jews ordered out, kept from leaving, and baptized by force, some of whom kept their Judaism in secret. Today's word.
Your line: they tried not to forget. Some kept their prayers by heart into the twentieth century. Day nine hundred forty-eight, done.

howItsDone: Jews remember the forced conversions in Spain and Portugal in history and story, and some descendants of New Christian families today study their roots and return to Jewish life.
